reviewers.summary: The scope ordering now makes the sign-in test distinguish retaining cp-case-b from falling back to the first scope. It still does not cover the non-null session-change handler identified in the prior finding.

findingList.message: The prior test-coverage finding remains: exercise a non-null session change while cp-case-b is selected and cp-case-a is first in the new session’s scopes, then assert cp-case-b remains active.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test signs out and signs back in through the sign-in flow. That flow resolves the selected case separately; the test does not invoke handleSessionChange with a non-null session.
evidence.failureScenario: If handleSessionChange regresses to always selecting the first scope, this test can still pass because it exercises sign-in instead of that handler. A session update while cp-case-b is selected could therefore switch to cp-case-a without detection.

reviewers.summary: The prior test finding is resolved: the test selects cp-case-b, changes sessions while that selection remains active, puts cp-case-a first in the next session, and asserts cp-case-b remains selected. The production session-change path preserves the selection across sign-out and resolves it against the next session.
The changed session-selection behavior has no test that catches the previously reported regression. I found no concrete security vulnerability in the reviewed code.

findingList.message: The prior test-coverage finding remains unresolved: this test does not verify retaining an in-scope active case across a non-null session change. Change the test to update the session while cp-case-b is selected, list cp-case-a first in the next session’s scopes, and assert cp-case-b remains active.

evidence.codePathTraced: The test changes sessions by signing out and then signing in again. The prior round identifies that sign-out clears the selected case, so this does not exercise retaining a selected case during a non-null session change.
evidence.failureScenario: If the session-change handler always selects the first case scope, this test can still pass because it does not preserve cp-case-b through a non-null session update with cp-case-a listed first.
